# Imposing a code breaks the symmetry of forms

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`imposing-a-code-breaks-the-symmetry` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](imposing-a-code-breaks-the-symmetry.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> For any family and any forms, imposing one code makes all agree in a step, keeps every exchange of formations and keeps no renaming that moves a form it gives: agreement from symmetry without a formation above the others.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Imposing a code keeps every exchange of formations; where a renaming moves the form the code gives some sense, imposing does not keep that renaming. (`Becoming.SharedCodes.impose_keeps_exchange`, `Becoming.SharedCodes.impose_privileges_forms`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom; any type of formations, senses and forms.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- That a code is in fact imposed, or that imposing is better than another way to agree.

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · A law of the formal model; its correspondence to actual systems is a separate obligation. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · A relation omitted by a weaker description does not refute the fuller account.
